answer: Each epoch, identities draft into one of several reward pools with capped membership, each pool's fixed payout split among its members. A sybil farmer cannot profitably stack one pool: every added puppet dilutes its own siblings' share until the pool runs hollow, and commitments are public so rivals see the fleet's weight and counter-position. Spreading across pools forces one operator to win several contests with divided attention. The opal wins its setting by taking a side: one identity, one bet, publicly committed — and the harbor shelters only ships that sailed under their own flag.
